action.about: Something a user runs on an object: a menu row, a palette entry or a key. A surface places it by id.

block.about: A copyable block (code, a command, a log, a file excerpt): Copy, Send to terminal and Add to composer derive from it.

condition.about: A simulated real-life state (a slow link, a usage limit, a huge diff): one simulator induces it, a stage puts the app into it, one measure says whether it holds, and every surface its walks visit needs a case.

scaffold.entry:
export const {{name}} = define.condition({
	id: "{{id}}",
	group: "real-life",
	said: { date: "{{date}}", quote: "{{said}}", where: "{{where}}" },
	appliesTo: { walks: "all", categories: [] },
	simulator: "unbuilt",
	profile: {},
	measure: [],
	verdict: "reviewed",
	ci: { debt: "climb" },
	status: "parked",
});

lens.about: A holistic review angle (security, CI cost, test honesty, settings defaults): it groups conditions or names a check, and carries the reviewer's rubric. It has no pass/fail of its own.

setting.about: A setting: its page and anchor, its name and sentence for search, its stored key, and the surfaces it shapes.

surface.about: An object on screen with menus: right-click, its ⋯ and the palette list the actions it places. Rendered as <Surface id>.

check.measure: median job minutes per workflow over the last 3 runs, and CI using fake agents only
check.budget: ratchet rows measure/ci-minutes: they only fall

fields.rubric: Per-PR CI runs only the cells the diff touches, nightly runs the rest, and CI spends no real tokens: fake agents only.

said.quote: what was the verdict about our tests lying? Are we good there?
said.where: operator, organizer session, 2026-11-10 09:12Z

check.measure: hits of the three test rules (bare assertion, expect inside a branch or mock, early return), tests that match nothing, mutation score, and retyped thresholds
check.budget: ratchet rows tests.lint and measure/*: they only fall

fields.rubric: A test asserts every claim in its name, the exact value the behaviour produces, and fails when it cannot set up its condition. A passing run with no tests matched is a failure.

said.quote: I want to do and build a comparable app, we first get a good enough app out and then worry about the small small security details
said.where: operator, security review triage

check.measure: simulated attacks failing, high advisories (with dependency-audit.yml) and open findings that are cheap, serious and reachable

fields.rubric: Fix now only a finding that is reachable without effort, does real harm and has a small fix; every other one goes to the one security backlog issue.

said.quote: each integration point that we add is more technical debt that we have to maintain
said.where: operator, organizer session, 2026-11-10 09:12Z

fields.rubric: Parked. An integration is cheap to add, update and remove, and a break shows up as a disabled integration, not as silence.

said.quote: game-feel without gamification
said.where: organizer relay of the operator, 2026-11-04 (ui-reset PROMPT.md); verbatim unconfirmed

fields.rubric: Parked. Ease and flow: a first win in under a minute, instant feedback, one obvious next step. No streaks, points, badges or leaderboards.

said.quote: Why do all our texts and icons look jagged and not production grade?
said.where: operator, organizer session, 2026-11-12 15:40Z

fields.rubric: Look at DPR-2 shots at 1600 px and at phone width: text, icons and borders are crisp and look production grade. A 1x shot proves nothing.

said.quote: having good default settings and adding controls in settings section
said.where: operator, organizer session, 2026-11-11 08:46Z

fields.rubric: Every setting ships with a default that works without opening Settings, a control, and a one-line description; a feature that adds behaviour adds its setting in the same change.

said.quote: what about clearing things up automatically when a thread is settled or marked done
said.where: operator, organizer session, 2026-11-11 08:40Z; also 2026-11-10 10:12Z, many node.exe left running

fields.rubric: Settling or finishing a thread ends everything it started: watches, crons, worktrees, child threads and processes. Look for what is still running afterwards.
